title: Sunshine Atlas: monthly sunshine scores and climate normals for 3,833 airport-served destinations
description:
Monthly 0–100 Sunshine Scores, average day/night temperatures, rainfall and sea-surface temperature for 3,833 destinations worldwide — every destination served by its own airport (one primary airport per metro area). Derived from long-term climate normals, not forecasts, by Sunshine Atlas.

Files: sunshine-atlas-destinations.csv — one row per destination (identity, coordinates, elevation, population, climate band, destination type, annual sunshine hours, annual rainfall mm, best month, year + 12 monthly Sunshine Scores); sunshine-atlas-monthly-climate.csv — one row per destination-month (45,996 rows: score, day high °C, night low °C, rain mm, sea temperature °C); sunshine-atlas-destinations.json — both combined, with per-destination page URLs. Join key: iata.

The Sunshine Score combines daytime warmth (ideal 20–32 °C), dryness and annual sunshine hours into one 0–100 number per destination-month: methodology. The canonical, always-current copy is sunshineatlas.com/data/; this record is the 2026.11.1 edition. Also on Hugging Face, and queryable live by AI assistants via MCP.

Changed in 2026.11.1: the climate values, checked against the WMO 1991–2020 climate normals (NOAA NCEI accession 0253808) at the stations within 15 km and 150 m of an atlas airport, and corrected. Day highs read 0.85 °C too cold and night lows 0.70 °C too warm (a 50 km grid cell has a narrower day than an airport's open ground); they are now corrected by an amount that runs smoothly with latitude (highs +1.8 °C near the equator, +0.5 to +0.7 °C further out; lows −0.4 to −0.8 °C), fitted by cross-validation by station: the error fell from 1.45 to 1.16 °C for highs (1,453 stations) and from 1.48 to 1.40 °C for lows. Rainfall is now 0.94 × (0.8 × CHELSA V2.1 + 0.2 × NASA POWER), CHELSA's 1981–2010 climatology at about 1 km (Karger et al., CC0): against 1,450 stations the monthly error fell from 19.7 to 12.2 mm and the annual from 201 to 117 mm, with no bias. Sunshine hours use Ångström–Prescott coefficients fitted to measured sunshine (0.19 and 0.62 instead of FAO-56's 0.25 and 0.50, which overstated about 100 h/yr): against 410 published figures the MAE fell from 212 to 190 h/yr, at the WMO stations from 225 to 185. Every Sunshine Score, best month and destination type was recomputed (the best month changed for 1,448 destinations). No column, row or page URL changed. The station normals are used to fit and measure only; none is redistributed here.

Changed in 2026.11: adds one column, duplicate_of_iata (duplicateOfIata in the JSON). Nine metros are served by two airports and so hold two rows; the column is empty on every primary and carries the primary's code on each second row, so filtering it empty returns exactly one row per place (3,824 of 3,833). Both rows remain, because each carries the climate of its own coordinates. Additive only: no existing value, column order or page URL changed, and climate values are identical to 2026.10. Also corrects the published accuracy figures for the modelled sunshine hours: the validation now matches 410 met-service cities with a bias of +24 h/yr, not the 404 and +22 h/yr stated in earlier editions; correlation (0.92) and MAE (212 h/yr) are unchanged. The earlier figures were correct when written and drifted as destination names were corrected in 2026.09 and 2026.10, which let more cities match the reference list.

Changed in 2026.10: adds a midday UV index (peak per destination, and per destination-month) on the WHO scale, from the same NASA POWER climatology as the rest. Disambiguates 22 destinations that shared a name with a different place — Portland (Maine) vs Portland, Oregon; Victoria (Seychelles) vs Victoria (British Columbia); London (Ontario); Birmingham (Alabama); Manchester (New Hampshire); St. Petersburg (Florida); Kochi (Japan); Jackson Hole; Hamilton Island — and corrects two labels to the place the airport serves (RUN to Saint-Denis (Réunion), SMS to Île Sainte-Marie). No iata changed; joins and page URLs are unaffected and climate values are identical to 2026.09. Nine metros legitimately hold two rows (LHR/SEN, GLA/PIK, MEL/MEB, SEA/PAE, YUL/YHU, KEF/RKV, MMY/SHI, ULV/ULY, BZI/EDO) — the README names them so they can be deduplicated.

Changed in 2026.09: 118 destination names corrected where the record carried the airport's host municipality instead of the destination the airport serves (Gaziemir → Izmir, Årø → Molde, Ciudad de la Costa → Montevideo, Beringin → Medan, plus typo fixes and island-convention labels such as La Gomera, Elba, Ixtapa-Zihuatanejo and Ancona), and 146 population figures corrected to describe the named place itself rather than an inherited catchment or neighbouring-city figure (GeoNames populations, with commonly-quoted census figures where the label is an island, region or metro). Page URLs are unchanged; climate values are identical to 2026.08.

Changed in 2026.08: temperature, rainfall and sunshine now derive from NASA POWER's January 2001 – December 2020 climatology throughout. Earlier editions anchored temperatures to, and modelled sunshine from, CRU CL v2.0 — a 1961–1990 normal — producing a hybrid series with no single reference period. Temperatures are now corrected for the difference between a grid cell's mean elevation and the destination's own using the standard 6.5 °C/km lapse rate; sunshine hours are modelled from POWER's all-sky clearness index via the Ångström–Prescott relation and each month's true astronomical daylength. The rainy_days_per_year column is replaced by annual_rainfall_mm: POWER reports precipitation depth, not wet-day frequency, and that column was not worth guessing.

Provenance: every value is either a measurement from the sources below or computed from them by a formula documented on the methodology page. Nothing in this dataset is written, estimated or filled in by a language model. Three caveats: annual_sunshine_hours is modelled, not observed — validated against the WMO 1991–2020 normals at 517 stations (MAE 185 h/yr) and 410 published national met-service figures (r = 0.92, MAE 190 h/yr, bias −31 h/yr), with Ångström–Prescott coefficients fitted to them, and it reads high where persistent low marine cloud or dust sits under the satellite's view (Lima and Cape Verde ~35–40% over) and low in the overcast Sichuan basin, a known limitation of satellite-derived sunshine (Kothe et al. 2017, Remote Sensing 9(5), 429); sunshine hours above roughly 60°N inland are unreliable and read high — above the Arctic Circle the model returns a median of about 2,140 h/yr, higher than the band beneath it, with only one of those 73 destinations having a published figure to check against and the two high-latitude cities that do (Tromsø, Iqaluit) both about 500 h over; the maritime sub-Arctic reads modestly high (Iceland ~1,490 against 1,326 measured at Reykjavík, coastal Norway ~1,540) while continental Canada (~2,230), Alaska (~1,940) and Russia (~1,980) inflate badly, most likely because snow and sea-ice albedo defeat the clearness retrieval; sea_temp_c is a single year (2024), not a normal; climate and destination_type are rule-based classifications and sunshine_score is an opinionated index, not measurements.

Also corrected in 2026.08: the continent column. It previously came from Wikidata per-airport, was absent for 25% of destinations and silently defaulted to Asia — Fiji, Greenland, the Bahamas and 157 Canadian airports all shipped as "Asia" — and was unreliable where present (Bilbao and Girona as Africa, Chaniá on Crete as Asia, Novosibirsk as Europe). It is now derived from OurAirports' country-to-continent table plus explicit geographic rules for the six transcontinental countries (Urals for Russia, Bosphorus for Turkey, Ural river for Kazakhstan, Canaries and Melilla to Africa, Sinai to Asia, Hawaii to Oceania).

Upstream sources: temperature and sunshine from NASA POWER climatology, 2001–2020 (CC BY 4.0), the day highs, night lows and sunshine coefficients corrected to the WMO 1991–2020 station normals; rainfall a blend of CHELSA V2.1 (Karger et al., 1981–2010, CC0) and NASA POWER; place data © GeoNames & OurAirports (CC BY); elevations from the Copernicus DEM via Open-Meteo; sea temperatures via Open-Meteo Marine (CC BY 4.0).
